items.title: The pi-adic completion of a localization of an integral perfectoid ring is again integral perfectoid
items.author: Juan Esteban Rodríguez Camargo
items.work: An integral model of the perfectoid modular curve
items.source_version: Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 8 (2021), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.170
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an integral perfectoid ring R with pseudo-uniformizer pi and any f in R, the pi-adic completion R<f^{-1}> = lim_n R/pi^n[f^{-1}] is again an integral perfectoid ring (statement lines 469-472). The proof computes the completion from the short exact sequences obtained by multiplying by pi^k - possible because pi is not a zero divisor - localizes them at f and passes to the inverse limit, which gives both pi-adic completeness and the non-zero-divisor property, and then localizes the Frobenius isomorphism at f to get surjectivity of the Frobenius on R<f^{-1}>/pi (proof lines 475-488). The step that carries the content is the passage from the level-wise sequences to the limit, since that is what identifies the completion of the localization with the localized completion and transfers both defining properties; the Frobenius check is then immediate by localizing an isomorphism. H2.
